title: Ten Years for a Necklace
subtitle: 為了一條項鍊付出十年：莫泊桑〈項鍊〉
source: 原創導讀；小說原文依 Project Gutenberg《Complete Original Short Stories of Guy de Maupassant》英譯〈The Diamond Necklace〉（公版），背景依 Wikipedia〈The Necklace〉，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Guy de Maupassant, “The Diamond Necklace”, Complete Original Short Stories, Project Gutenberg

beginner.title: The Borrowed Necklace
paras: Mathilde Loisel is a pretty young woman in Paris. Her husband is a clerk, and they do not have much money. Mathilde is always unhappy. She dreams of beautiful dresses, expensive jewels and a rich life. She feels she was born for luxury.
瑪蒂爾德．盧瓦塞爾是巴黎一位漂亮的年輕女子。她的丈夫是個小職員，他們沒什麼錢。瑪蒂爾德總是不快樂。她夢想著漂亮的衣服、昂貴的珠寶和富裕的生活。她覺得自己生來就該享受奢華。

One day, her husband brings home an invitation to a grand party at the minister’s home. Mathilde cries because she has nothing to wear. Her husband gives her four hundred francs that he was saving for a gun, so she buys a new dress. But she still has no jewels. Her husband says she could wear fresh flowers, but she says nothing is worse than looking poor among rich women.
有一天，丈夫帶回一張邀請函，是部長府邸舉辦的盛大舞會。瑪蒂爾德哭了，因為她沒有衣服可穿。丈夫把原本存來買槍的四百法郎給了她，她便買了一件新禮服。但她還是沒有珠寶。丈夫說她可以戴鮮花，但她說，沒有什麼比在有錢女人之中顯得寒酸更丟臉了。

She borrows a diamond necklace from her rich friend, Madame Forestier. At the party, Mathilde looks beautiful, and everyone admires her. But when she gets home, the necklace is gone! They search everywhere, but they cannot find it.
她向有錢的朋友佛萊斯蒂埃夫人借了一條鑽石項鍊。在舞會上，瑪蒂爾德美麗動人，人人都欣賞她。但回到家時，項鍊不見了！他們到處找，卻怎麼也找不到。

Too ashamed to tell her friend, they buy a similar necklace for thirty-six thousand francs. They borrow most of the money. For ten long years, they work very hard to pay it back. Mathilde does heavy housework and becomes old and tired. When Mathilde returns the necklace, her friend does not even open the box.
因為太羞愧而不敢告訴朋友，他們花了三萬六千法郎買了一條相似的項鍊，大部分的錢都是借來的。整整十年，他們拚命工作來還債。瑪蒂爾德做著粗重的家事，變得又老又疲憊。瑪蒂爾德歸還項鍊時，朋友連盒子都沒打開。

After ten years, Mathilde meets Madame Forestier in the street and tells her the truth. Her friend is shocked. “Oh, my poor Mathilde!” she says. The necklace was not real diamonds. It was worth at most five hundred francs! This 1884 story is famous for its surprise ending.
十年後，瑪蒂爾德在街上遇見佛萊斯蒂埃夫人，告訴她真相。她的朋友大吃一驚。「噢，我可憐的瑪蒂爾德！」她說。那條項鍊根本不是真鑽石，頂多只值五百法郎！這個 1884 年的故事以出人意料的結局聞名。

intermediate.title: Ten Years for a Necklace
paras: Guy de Maupassant’s “The Necklace”, first published in the French newspaper Le Gaulois on 17 February 1884, introduces us to Mathilde Loisel, a pretty young woman married to a clerk at the Ministry of Education. Although she lives comfortably enough, she suffers constantly, feeling that she was “born to enjoy all delicacies and all luxuries” and dreaming of a wealth she will never have.
莫泊桑的〈項鍊〉於 1884 年 2 月 17 日首次刊登於法國的《高盧人報》，故事主角是瑪蒂爾德．盧瓦塞爾，一位嫁給教育部小職員的漂亮年輕女子。雖然生活還算過得去，她卻總是受苦，覺得自己「生來就該享受一切珍饈與奢華」，夢想著一種她永遠得不到的財富。

When her husband proudly brings home an invitation to a ball given by the minister, two great tears run down Mathilde’s cheeks, because she has nothing suitable to wear. He gives her the four hundred francs he had been saving to buy a gun. With her new dress, she still feels poor without jewels, so she borrows a diamond necklace from a wealthy friend, Madame Forestier. Her husband suggests wearing fresh roses, which would cost only ten francs, but she refuses: nothing, she says, is more humiliating than looking poor among rich women.
丈夫驕傲地帶回部長舉辦的舞會邀請函時，瑪蒂爾德臉頰上卻滑下兩行淚，因為她沒有合適的衣服。丈夫把原本存來買槍的四百法郎給了她。有了新禮服，她仍然覺得沒有珠寶顯得寒酸，於是向有錢的朋友佛萊斯蒂埃夫人借了一條鑽石項鍊。丈夫建議她戴只要十法郎的新鮮玫瑰，但她拒絕了：她說，沒有什麼比在有錢女人之中顯得寒酸更丟臉了。

At the ball, Mathilde is a triumph, admired by everyone. But at home, she discovers that the necklace is missing. After searching everywhere in vain, the couple decide not to admit the loss. They find a nearly identical necklace costing thirty-six thousand francs. Monsieur Loisel uses an inheritance from his father and borrows the rest at high interest. When Mathilde returns it, Madame Forestier coldly says she should have brought it back sooner — and never opens the case.
舞會上，瑪蒂爾德大獲成功，人人都欣賞她。但回到家，她發現項鍊不見了。到處搜尋卻徒勞無功之後，這對夫妻決定不承認遺失這件事。他們找到一條幾乎一模一樣、要價三萬六千法郎的項鍊。盧瓦塞爾先生動用了父親留下的遺產，其餘的則以高利借款補足。瑪蒂爾德歸還時，佛萊斯蒂埃夫人冷冷地說她應該早點還——而且始終沒有打開盒子。

Their life changes completely. They dismiss their maid and move to a cheap apartment. Mathilde learns “what heavy housework meant”: washing dishes, carrying water up the stairs and bargaining over every coin. Her husband works evenings copying documents. This life lasts ten years, and by the end, Mathilde has lost her youthful beauty.
他們的生活徹底改變。他們辭退女傭，搬進一間廉價公寓。瑪蒂爾德學會了「粗重家務是什麼滋味」：洗碗、提水上樓、為每一分錢討價還價。她的丈夫晚上兼差抄寫文件。這種生活持續了十年，到最後，瑪蒂爾德已失去了青春的美貌。

One Sunday, she meets Madame Forestier and, proud that the debt is paid, tells her everything. Her friend, deeply moved, takes her hands: “Oh, my poor Mathilde! Why, my necklace was paste! It was worth at most only five hundred francs!” The twist ending, a hallmark of Maupassant’s style, forces readers to ask whether Mathilde was ruined by bad luck, by pride, or by her refusal to tell the truth.
一個星期天，她遇見佛萊斯蒂埃夫人，為了債務已經還清而感到自豪，便把一切都告訴了她。她的朋友深受感動，握住她的手：「噢，我可憐的瑪蒂爾德！我那條項鍊是假的！頂多只值五百法郎！」這個轉折結局是莫泊桑風格的標誌，迫使讀者思考：毀了瑪蒂爾德的，究竟是壞運氣、虛榮，還是她不願說出真相？

advanced.title: Pride, Appearances and an Expensive Silence
paras: Guy de Maupassant’s “The Necklace”, published in Le Gaulois on 17 February 1884, is one of the most widely taught short stories in the world, largely because of its devastating final line. Yet the twist works only because the preceding pages have been constructed with such economy. In just a few thousand words, Maupassant creates a character, a social world and a moral trap from which there is no escape.
莫泊桑的〈項鍊〉於 1884 年 2 月 17 日刊登於《高盧人報》，是全世界最常被拿來教學的短篇小說之一，很大程度上要歸功於它毀滅性的最後一句話。然而，這個轉折之所以奏效，是因為前面的篇幅寫得極其精簡。短短幾千字裡，莫泊桑就塑造了一個角色、一個社會世界，以及一個無處可逃的道德陷阱。

Mathilde Loisel is introduced as one of those pretty and charming young women born, “as if by a slip of fate,” into a family of clerks. Married to a minor official at the Ministry of Public Instruction, she is not destitute, but she suffers “ceaselessly, feeling herself born to enjoy all delicacies and all luxuries.” Her unhappiness springs less from poverty than from comparison: she measures her life against an imagined world of wealth, and that measure makes everything she has seem inadequate.
瑪蒂爾德．盧瓦塞爾一出場，就是那種「彷彿命運失手」才出生在小職員家庭的漂亮迷人女子。她嫁給公共教育部的一名小官員，並非一貧如洗，卻「無休止地受苦，覺得自己生來就該享受一切珍饈與奢華」。她的不快樂，與其說來自貧窮，不如說來自比較：她拿自己的人生去和一個想像中的富裕世界相比，而這把尺讓她擁有的一切都顯得不足。

The invitation to the minister’s ball sets the trap. Her husband sacrifices the four hundred francs he had saved for a hunting gun so that she can buy a dress, and she borrows a diamond necklace from her wealthy friend, Madame Forestier. For one evening, she achieves the life she has imagined. Then the necklace disappears. Rather than confess the loss, the couple buy a replacement for thirty-six thousand francs, using an inheritance and borrowing the remainder at ruinous interest. When Mathilde returns it, Madame Forestier does not even open the case.
部長舞會的邀請函布下了陷阱。丈夫犧牲了原本存來買獵槍的四百法郎，讓她去買禮服；她則向有錢的朋友佛萊斯蒂埃夫人借了一條鑽石項鍊。那一晚，她實現了自己想像中的人生。接著，項鍊不見了。這對夫妻沒有坦承遺失，而是花三萬六千法郎買了一條替代品，動用了遺產，其餘則以毀滅性的高利借來。瑪蒂爾德歸還項鍊時，佛萊斯蒂埃夫人甚至沒有打開盒子。

The consequences unfold over a decade. The Loisels dismiss their maid and move into a garret; Mathilde scrubs greasy pans, carries water up the stairs and bargains for every sou, while her husband copies manuscripts late into the night. Maupassant pauses to let her reflect: “What would have happened if she had not lost that necklace? Who knows? who knows? How strange and changeful is life! How small a thing is needed to make or ruin us!” By the time the debt is cleared, she has aged prematurely, her beauty worn away by labour. Sometimes, alone by the window, she remembers the ball where she had been “so beautiful and so admired.”
後果在十年間逐步展開。盧瓦塞爾夫婦辭退女傭，搬進閣樓；瑪蒂爾德刷洗油膩的鍋子、提水上樓、為每一分錢討價還價，丈夫則熬夜抄寫手稿。莫泊桑在此稍作停頓，讓她回想：「如果她沒有弄丟那條項鍊，會發生什麼事呢？誰知道？誰知道？人生多麼奇妙又多變！成就或毀掉我們，只需要多麼微小的一件事！」等到債務還清時，她已提早衰老，美貌被勞苦磨蝕殆盡。有時，她獨自坐在窗邊，回想起那場她曾「如此美麗、如此受人讚賞」的舞會。

The final revelation reframes everything. Meeting Madame Forestier by chance, Mathilde proudly explains the sacrifice — only to learn that the original necklace was paste, worth at most five hundred francs. The irony is layered. The Loisels destroyed ten years to preserve an appearance of respectability, protecting a reputation that a single honest conversation would have saved. Readers continue to debate whether Mathilde is punished for vanity, defeated by chance, or quietly redeemed by the hard-working dignity she discovers. That the story supports all three readings is part of what has kept it alive for well over a century.

最後的揭露讓一切都被重新詮釋。瑪蒂爾德偶然遇見佛萊斯蒂埃夫人，驕傲地說出這份犧牲——卻得知原本那條項鍊是假的，頂多只值五百法郎。這個反諷是多層次的：盧瓦塞爾夫婦為了維持體面的表象，毀掉了十年；他們保護的名聲，其實只要一次誠實的對話就能保住。讀者至今仍在爭論，瑪蒂爾德究竟是因虛榮受罰、敗給了機運，還是因她在勞苦中發現的尊嚴而默默得到了救贖。這個故事能同時支持三種解讀，正是它流傳一百多年仍歷久彌新的原因之一。
